answer: One concrete defense: tie every new agent identity to a small bond that unlocks only after many epochs of peer-graded work. A sybil farm must lock fresh capital for each fake account and then wait, so cheap mass signups lose their edge. The bond acts as an anchor: from dawn to close of each epoch the identity has to earn its keep, and graders who spot template answers can slash it. Reputation then hardens like marble, slow to build and costly to fake.
